findings.quote: both because the gift seemed worthy of gratitude and because the expense appeared to amount to not much less than ten talents
findings.problem: The Greek sentence about cost is a separate bracketed gloss, [δοκεῖ γὰρ ἡ δαπάνη οὐ πολὺ λείπειν τῶν δέκα ταλάντων], 'for the cost seems to fall little short of ten talents'. It is not a second reason given by the Achaeans, and the editorial brackets (a suspected interpolation) are silently dropped.
findings.proposed_fix: because the gift seemed worthy of gratitude. [For the cost seems to fall little short of ten talents.]

units.note: Bracketed sentence is a probable gloss in the Greek; the fix preserves the brackets.

findings.quote: on the pretext of keeping their own laws and decrees in force
findings.problem: Greek has χάριν τοῦ διαμένειν τοὺς νόμους ἰσχυροὺς καὶ τὰ δόγματα, 'for the sake of keeping the laws and decrees strong'. It states their purpose; there is no word for 'pretext'.
findings.proposed_fix: for the sake of keeping their own laws and decrees in force

findings.quote: And since the Achaean nation had grown and advanced in the best direction from the period covered by my history, this in turn became the beginning of its change for the worse: the audacity of Callicrates.
findings.problem: οὕτω δὲ τοῦ τῶν Ἀχαιῶν ἔθνους ηὐξημένου … αὕτη πάλιν ἀρχὴ … ἐγένετο μεταβολῆς is 'Thus, with the nation having grown … this again became the beginning of the change'. It is not causal 'since'. The Greek then breaks off after τὸ Καλλικράτους θράσος * with a marked lacuna, which the English smooths over.
findings.proposed_fix: Thus, with the Achaean nation having grown and advanced in the best direction from the period covered by my history, this in turn became the beginning of its change for the worse: the audacity of Callicrates [text lost here].

findings.problem: The Greek has a second lacuna (** Ῥωμαῖοι ὄντες ἄνθρωποι …) before this sentence. The passage begins mid-thought and is not a continuation of the Callicrates sentence, but the English reads on as if whole.

findings.quote: But whenever someone reminds them of what is just, having kept faith, they draw back
findings.problem: τετηρηκὼς τὴν πίστιν is nominative singular and agrees with τις ('someone who has kept faith'), not with the Romans. The English attaches it to the Romans.
findings.proposed_fix: But whenever someone who has kept faith reminds them of what is just, they draw back

findings.quote: to add to the other evils, he did so by bribery
findings.problem: πρὸς τοῖς ἄλλοις κακοῖς καὶ δωροδοκηθείς is passive, 'was bribed (took bribes)'. It does not say he won the office by bribing others, so the English reverses who paid whom.
findings.proposed_fix: besides his other misdeeds, he was himself bribed

findings.quote: Instead he said they must first make a legal case, and then press their claim again; and if even then they failed to persuade, one should at last yield under protest
findings.problem: Subject is the Achaeans: ἔφη δεῖν δικαιολογεῖσθαι, μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα πάλιν ἀξιοῦν, εἰ δὲ μηδ᾽ οὕτως πείθοιεν (the Romans). The English 'they' reads as the Romans making the case and failing to persuade, which makes no sense with 'one should yield'.
findings.proposed_fix: Instead he said that one must first plead one's case, and then make the request again; and if even so one failed to persuade the Romans, one should at last yield, calling witnesses to one's protest
